newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crudes hold above support levels on ACCESS.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crudes hold above support levels on ACCESS.

text.p: U.S. crude oil prices steadied above technical support levels in thin after-hours ACCESS trade, brokers said, with further declines seen Thursday.
"You saw a decent sell-off today in the crude...It'll continue tomorrow," one trader said.
He referred to the gasoline-led fall in NYMEX crude oil for November delivery, which closed nine cents lower a barrel at $24.05.
November NYMEX crude oil traded up slightly on ACCESS, touching $24.07 a barrel by 2100 EDT/0100 GMT. Technical support was seen at $24 and $23.80.
Meanwhile, gasoline pressured crude by falling 0.40 cent to 62.42 cents a gallon in daytime trade, following a second set of inventory data which showed builds last week.
November heating oil continued firming after-hours, adding 0.02 cents a gallon to its settle of 71.98 cents.
Heating oil ended the day 1.22 cents a gallon higher as the U.S. government reiterated Tuesday's industry reports of historically low supplies.
